name: tsdataclinic/newerhoods
what_it_holds: NYC Data Clinic project aggregating NYC Open Data at the census-tract level and using ML (clustering) to redraw data-driven neighbourhood boundaries; includes tract-level feature tables and boundary-generation code, Apache-2.0.
why_useful: Provides both a census-tract-level NYC dataset and a method for building STR-relevant neighbourhood definitions from tract data, useful for any tract-to-neighbourhood crosswalk work on NYC STR data.
themes: Geocoding, neighbourhood boundaries and census-tract crosswalks used for STR studies; city GIS portals with STR layers
why_all: Provides both a census-tract-level NYC dataset and a method for building STR-relevant neighbourhood definitions from tract data, useful for any tract-to-neighbourhood crosswalk work on NYC STR data.

name: hantswilliams/hud_usps_crosswalk_files
what_it_holds: Committed copies of HUD-USPS ZIP-code crosswalk files (ZIP to census tract / county / CBSA), which HUD otherwise only distributes as a paid/registration-gated quarterly download.
why_useful: A free mirror of the standard ZIP<->tract/county/CBSA crosswalk used to join STR registry data (often ZIP-level) to census geographies for regional aggregation; generally useful infrastructure for any of our municipal STR registry work.
themes: Geocoding, neighbourhood boundaries and census-tract crosswalks used for STR studies; city GIS portals with STR layers
why_all: A free mirror of the standard ZIP<->tract/county/CBSA crosswalk used to join STR registry data (often ZIP-level) to census geographies for regional aggregation; generally useful infrastructure for any of our municipal STR registry work.

name: kraina-ai/QuackOSM
what_it_holds: Open-source Python/CLI tool (375 stars, Apache-2.0) for reading OpenStreetMap PBF extracts directly via DuckDB, producing tabular/geoparquet output of OSM features (including tourism/accommodation/POI tags) for any region.
why_useful: A one-command way to pull OSM points of interest (hotels, short-term-rental-tagged buildings, restaurants/attractions used as tourism-density proxies) for any city/country as a free, always-current geospatial layer feeding gap #20 (geospatial POI / party-size proxies) and cross-checking Inside Airbnb listing density against broader tourism infrastructure.
time_coverage: current OSM snapshot, any historical PBF extract if available
last_activity: active (390+375 stars across kraina-ai repos, actively maintained per repo listing)
themes: Data-hosting mirrors pointed at from GitHub: Zenodo, Figshare, Harvard Dataverse, HuggingFace, Kaggle, Mendeley Data collections on Airbnb, STR, hotels, tourism
why_all: A one-command way to pull OSM points of interest (hotels, short-term-rental-tagged buildings, restaurants/attractions used as tourism-density proxies) for any city/country as a free, always-current geospatial layer feeding gap #20 (geospatial POI / party-size proxies) and cross-checking Inside Airbnb listing density against broader tourism infrastructure.

name: popFlowEstonia
what_it_holds: Leaflet/D3 population-flowmap visualization built on an origin-destination (OD) matrix derived from mobile positioning data supplied by the University of Tartu Mobility Lab (the academic group behind Positium, Estonia's mobile-network-operator tourism-statistics pioneer that feeds Eurostat's MNO experimental statistics work). Contains a committed data file data/population_estonia.js (~11.1MB) holding the OD matrix/flow data for Estonia, plus index.html/style.css for the map viewer.
why_useful: Directly touches the Eurostat MNO-experimental-statistics lineage named in this theme (Estonia/Positium/University of Tartu is the flagship MNO-tourism-stats case study); the committed 11MB OD-matrix file is real mobile-positioning-derived flow data, even though it is a population/commuting flow map rather than an inbound-tourism arrivals series, and no README detail on vintage/exact fields was retrievable via fetch.
themes: Electricity, water and waste data as occupancy proxies (smart-meter open data, tourist-area utility consumption), and mobile-phone tourism statistics (Eurostat MNO experimental)
why_all: Directly touches the Eurostat MNO-experimental-statistics lineage named in this theme (Estonia/Positium/University of Tartu is the flagship MNO-tourism-stats case study); the committed 11MB OD-matrix file is real mobile-positioning-derived flow data, even though it is a population/commuting flow map rather than an inbound-tourism arrivals series, and no README detail on vintage/exact fields was retrievable via fetch.

Directly downstream of the Estonian mobile-positioning/MNO tourism-statistics ecosystem the Eurostat experimental series is built on; if the OD matrices in data/ are real (not synthetic demo), this is a rare committed MNO-derived mobility dataset rather than just a paper describing the method.

name: reverse-engineering-YJMob100K-grid
what_it_holds: Code (65 commits) reverse-engineering the geographic grid underlying YJMob100K, a large anonymized human-mobility dataset (~100,000 users, ~75 days, originally Japan/Yahoo Japan) hosted on Zenodo; this repo's own outputs are a reproduced GeoJSON grid (EPSG:2449), choropleth maps, and comparative grids for Helsinki/London/Toronto/Dallas-Fort Worth, cross-validated against Japan's 2020 Census. Points to the YJMob100K Zenodo dataset itself for raw data. Code: BSD-3-Clause; figures: CC BY 4.0; shapefiles: OSM ODbL.
why_useful: YJMob100K is a substantial, real, publicly hosted (Zenodo) mobile-location panel that could proxy domestic mobility/tourism intensity in Japan (APAC gap) and other cities; this repo supplies the georeferencing/grid-reconstruction method needed to use it, and documents that de-identified location data does not anonymize well, which is itself a usable caveat for any mobile-positioning occupancy-proxy work.
geography: Japan (primary), plus Helsinki, London, Toronto, Dallas-Fort Worth grids
time_coverage: ~75 days of underlying YJMob100K panel (exact years not stated in fetch)
size_hint: ~100,000 users in underlying Zenodo dataset; this repo is grid/code only
themes: Electricity, water and waste data as occupancy proxies (smart-meter open data, tourist-area utility consumption), and mobile-phone tourism statistics (Eurostat MNO experimental)
why_all: YJMob100K is a substantial, real, publicly hosted (Zenodo) mobile-location panel that could proxy domestic mobility/tourism intensity in Japan (APAC gap) and other cities; this repo supplies the georeferencing/grid-reconstruction method needed to use it, and documents that de-identified location data does not anonymize well, which is itself a usable caveat for any mobile-positioning occupancy-proxy work.

Points to YJMob100K as an external, sizeable Japan urban-mobility dataset derived from mobile positioning; not tourism-labeled but could proxy visitor movement in a market (Japan/APAC) that is one of our numbered regional gaps if cross-referenced with known tourist areas.
